text:
lee: hey — I'm trying to pull the raw logs for request_id=01f3a9b2c4. I can see a trace id (trace: 2bf4-9c3d) in Tempo but the Console log search returns nothing. where should I look?

sasha: for prod, open Console > Observability > Logs. Try the structured field search: `req_id:01f3a9b2c4` (or `http.request_id:01f3a9b2c4`). console defaults to last 15m so expand the timerange.

lee: ah right didn't realize the time window. i expanded to 24h still nothing — the trace exists though. is there a direct map between trace id and logs?

james: traces don't always contain the full log payload. we add request_id as a span tag called `req_id` and also emit it in structured logs under `req_id` or `http.request_id`. If the app logs aren't showing the field, try a broader search: `service:frontend AND "01f3a9b2c4"` or grep the message text.

ana: fwiw you can also use the CLI if that's faster:
```
ri logs query --env prod --filter "req_id=01f3a9b2c4" --from "24h" --format json
```
That will hit the logs index directly and show raw lines.

sasha: another tip: if the logs were forwarded to the long-term index the Console alias might be different (logs_prod -> logs_prod_2026_*). CLI uses index aliases so it usually finds them.

james: if you only have trace id, open the trace in Tempo, expand the top-level span attributes — sometimes the request_id is attached. Example: open trace, click first span -> attributes -> request_id.

lee: great — the trace did have `req_id` in attributes. pulled with the CLI command and found the log lines. thanks! :tada:

monitoring-bot: Alert: high error rate detected on service/frontend at 2026-03-17T15:04:12Z — linked trace 2bf4-9c3d - incident created: INC-3241

james: one more note — if logs are missing entirely it might be sampling or a misconfigured logger. ping @ana and include the request_id+trace and we'll grep the ingress host and check ingestion pipeline. :+1:
